title: Total-evidence phylogeny and morphological character performance in tube-snouted electric fishes (Gymnotiformes: Sternarchorhynchus): systematics and historical biogeography of the Guianas
content:
Abstract
We investigate how anatomical characters perform across phylogenetic depth in a species-rich Neotropical radiation, using the tube-snouted electric fish genus Sternarchorhynchus as a model system. Using a total-evidence framework that integrates molecular and morphological data, we analyse 31 of the 34 recognized species. Phylogenetic relationships were inferred primarily under Bayesian inference, with parsimony-based analyses used diagnostically to evaluate the biological meaning of morphological signal and homoplasy. Discrete morphological characters provide a strong and coherent signal at deep phylogenetic levels, robustly supporting the monophyly of Sternarchorhynchus and its two principal species groups. In contrast, relationships within the species-rich Sternarchorhynchus mormyrus group show limited morphological resolution owing to pervasive homoplasy concentrated in feeding-related structures. This pattern reveals repeated functional convergence under strong ecological and mechanical constraints. Using this approach, we revise the systematics of Guianese Sternarchorhynchus, recognize four regional lineages, and describe a new rapids-dwelling species from the Oyapock River. Ancestral-area and habitat reconstructions indicate multiple dispersal events from the Amazon basin into the Guianas, followed by repeated ecological transitions between deep channels and rapids. Our results demonstrate that morphological homoplasy in species-rich fish radiations records ecological processes that shape lineage diversification.
